title: Align quotas/billing hooks to Standard Cost Model primitives + document intentional differences
creator: Talia Benson
description:
Problem
- Today Console/Optimize are converging on a Standard Cost Model spec + API, but quotas enforcement and billing hooks still use a separate set of token/cost primitives.
- This causes discrepancies between:
  (a) Console “cost breakdown” views
  (b) Optimize “what-if savings” projections
  (c) internal finance/unit economics reporting
  (d) customer invoice line items and quota burn
- We need quotas/billing hooks to be powered by the same canonical primitives so “what counts” is consistent, while explicitly documenting intentional differences where billing must diverge (e.g., pricing plans, rounding, credits, contractual adjustments).

Goal
- Refactor quotas + billing hooks to consume Standard Cost Model primitives (schema v1), using the same token-attribution inputs and stage breakdown semantics (prefill/decode, cache, batch efficiency signals) where applicable.
- Provide a clear mapping layer from cost primitives -> billable units for invoicing (hosted API), and from primitives -> quota units for enforcement.
- Document (and test) any intentional differences so Support/Finance/Console can explain deltas and we can prevent drift regressions.

Non-goals
- Replacing billing/RevRec systems or changing customer-facing pricing plans.
- Introducing new invoice line items (unless explicitly approved by Finance + PM; out of scope for v1).

Primary owners/stakeholders
- Owner: Cole Summers (billing hooks integration)
- Platform/API: Ethan Park, Kaitlyn Nguyen
- Telemetry: Nadia Rahman, Logan Wright
- Finance/FP&A: Laura Bennett, Rishi Malhotra
- Console: Chloe Martin / Jada Williams (for explaining deltas and support workflows)
acceptance_criteria:
Functional
- Quota burn (hosted API) and billing hooks both ingest the same canonical request primitives used by the cost-model service/library (schema v1).
- For every request, billing hooks persist:
  - cost_model_spec_version (e.g., cost-model/v1)
  - input primitive snapshot (bounded, no PII)
  - derived billable units (input/output tokens or equivalent)
  - mapping_version (billing-mapping/v1) to make future changes auditable.
- Console can reconcile: “invoice tokens” vs “standard cost model request-attributable cost” with a documented explanation of differences.

Correctness / determinism
- Deterministic mapping function from primitives -> billable units for the same spec version + mapping version.
- Backfill/replay on golden fixtures shows no material change to invoiced totals for a representative set of tenants (unless explicitly approved + communicated).

Observability
- Emit metrics for:
  - billing_hook_primitive_missing_count (by field)
  - billing_hook_mapping_version_distribution
  - delta between billing-derived unit cost and cost-model-estimated request-attributable cost (aggregated)
  - telemetry lag impact indicators (so drift alerts don’t page spuriously)

Documentation
- Confluence page section or README update that enumerates intentional differences:
  - what billing includes/excludes vs cost-model breakdown
  - rounding policy
  - credit/minimum commit handling
  - contract pricing overrides
  - backfill/correction behavior

Rollout
- Feature-flagged rollout per environment (staging -> canary tenants -> broader).
- Safe fallback to legacy billing hook path if primitives are unavailable or validation fails (with alerting).
implementation_notes:
Proposed approach
1) Introduce a shared “billing mapping” module that consumes cost-model primitives:
   - Input: CostModelRequestPrimitives (schema v1) + tenant pricing context
   - Output: BillableUnitsV1 { billable_input_tokens, billable_output_tokens, billable_embeddings_units, … }
   - Versioned: billing-mapping/v1 (explicitly separate from cost-model spec version)

2) Align quota enforcement to the same derived BillableUnitsV1 where possible.
   - Quotas should remain defined in customer-facing units (e.g., tokens) even if internal cost modeling uses richer breakdown.

3) Persist both:
   - raw primitives (bounded and sanitized)
   - derived billable units
   to support auditability + reconciliation.

Key mapping rules (v1 proposal; confirm with Finance)
- billable_input_tokens = request.input_tokens_total
  - Clarify cache behavior: if request uses server-side prefix/KV cache, we still bill based on customer plan policy.
  - Default v1: billable_input_tokens reflect tokens provided by customer in the prompt (not internal cache hits), unless plan explicitly bills for cache reads (currently we do not).
- billable_output_tokens = request.decode_tokens_total
- Do not include overhead allocation categories as billable line items.
- Any cost-model fields related to batch efficiency, queue time, kernel path, quantization deltas are non-billable diagnostics; they may affect internal cost estimates but should not directly change token billing units.

Intentional differences to document (expected deltas)
- Billing vs standard cost:
  - Billing uses contract price tables, free credits, minimum commits, and invoice adjustments; cost-model returns internal estimated cost breakdown.
  - Billing rounds units according to invoicing rules (e.g., per 1K token blocks or cents precision) while cost-model returns high-precision floats.
  - Billing is based on finalized metering with late-arriving corrections; cost-model may use near-real-time telemetry and should expose “provisional” flags.
- Quotas vs billing:
  - Quotas may be stricter/earlier (enforcement at request time) while billing is post-hoc; document behavior during telemetry lag or retries.

Open questions
- Cache billing policy: confirm current stance for hosted API for prefix/KV cache hits (policy appears to be “don’t charge for internal cache reuse”). If incorrect, we need to update mapping rules and comms.
- Retries: ensure we don’t double-count billable units on upstream retry behavior (client retries vs internal hedging).
- Streaming: confirm token accounting boundaries for partial streams and aborted responses.

Testing plan
- Add unit tests for mapping module using golden fixtures from ENG-4831.
- Add an integration test that replays a small anonymized request log through:
  (a) legacy billing hook
  (b) new primitives-based mapping
  and asserts equivalence within approved tolerances (ideally exact equality for billable token counts).
- Add a canary dashboard comparing legacy vs new derived billable tokens per tenant/day.
rollout_plan:
Phase 0 (prep)
- Land mapping module behind a flag (billing_mapping_v1_enabled=false by default).
- Add dual-write mode in staging: compute both legacy and new, log deltas.

Phase 1 (staging)
- Enable for staging tenants and run replay/backfill validation.

Phase 2 (prod canary)
- Enable for 1–3 internal or friendly tenants (low spend) + monitor:
  - delta metrics
  - support ticket volume
  - any increase in quota enforcement errors

Phase 3 (gradual ramp)
- Expand by tenant cohorts; stop the ramp if delta > threshold or missing primitives spike.

Phase 4 (default)
- Make primitives-based path default; keep legacy path as emergency fallback for one release window.

Rollback
- Flip flag to disable mapping v1 and revert to legacy billing hook path; alert Finance if any invoices may be impacted.
comments: 2026-02-05 (Cole Summers): Initial pass at mapping rules. Strong preference to keep billing in customer-facing units (input/output tokens) and treat cost-model breakdown as non-billable diagnostics. Will add mapping_version and persist primitive snapshots for audit/replay.

2026-02-06 (Laura Bennett): Finance requirement: any change that could affect invoice totals needs (1) replay evidence, (2) explicit sign-off, and (3) a way to reconstruct billed units from stored metering. Also please document rounding/credits/adjustments as the primary reasons invoice totals won’t equal “request-attributable cost.”

2026-02-08 (Nadia Rahman): Telemetry contract note: prefill/decode split is stable now, but cache hit metrics may be delayed for some runtimes. Recommend billing mapping only depend on tokens_total fields, not cache hit rates, to avoid missing-field risk on request path.

2026-02-11 (Ethan Park): +1 on determinism and bounds. Make sure quota enforcement can run with bounded payload and without calling the cost-model service synchronously (library/embedded path). Console/Optimize can call the service; billing hooks should not add latency to hot path.

2026-02-14 (Chloe Martin): Console needs a single explanation string for the UI/help center: “Invoice totals reflect pricing/credits/rounding; Console cost breakdown reflects internal compute allocation.” Please add a short ‘customer-facing explanation’ section to the doc we can link Support to.

2026-02-19 (Cole Summers): Implemented dual-compute in staging (legacy + mapping v1). Early results: exact match on billable input/output tokens for non-streaming requests; streaming abort cases show small deltas due to legacy counting behavior. Filing follow-up to clarify streaming cut-off semantics and ensure both paths agree.

2026-02-22 (Rafael Mendes): From SRE: add an alert on missing primitives rate > 0.1% and ensure flag rollback is one click. Also consider telemetry lag: billing should not page on drift metrics; drift alerts are for cost-model monitoring, not invoice correctness.

2026-02-24 (Cole Summers): PR up for review (pr-28521). Remaining TODO before merge: update documentation section on intentional differences + add a small replay harness for 7-day sample dataset. Requesting review from Nadia (telemetry), Kaitlyn (tenancy/auth), Laura (Finance).
